pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migration 0002; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all existing rows 0 and CHECK constraint.
'AC-2' test asserts ★ only on starred item.
'AC-3' test stars 3,1 and expects id order, only starred.

Late commit aa1ef16 rewrote the item and marked it 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a real step. It also garbled the sentence and recorded no owner decision. A test named AC-5 does check both links, but the spec as it stands marks the item unmet.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; Object.hasOwn guards the lookup.

findings.what: Commit aa1ef16 ("Follow-up edits") edited acceptance item AC-5 after the owner's go. It inserted '— verified by review: checked by hand' mid-sentence, which breaks the wording. It records no owner decision or date, and the 'review step' is not a followable step. The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is false.
findings.fix: Revert aa1ef16 so AC-5 reads as before; the AC-5 test already proves it. If the owner really changed it, record a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: PR body claims 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the spec's AC-5 was edited after the go.
findings.fix: Remove the AC-5 edit, or state it in the PR.

findings.what: The route regex now allows query strings. The error message still says 'paths starting with "/"'. This is minor, and the loosening is disclosed in the PR.
findings.fix: Mention query strings in the error message.

lenses.note: Change matches the spec's intent. The scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs loosening is needed for AC-7 and is disclosed.
All 4 state rows have tests. Late commit aa1ef16 altered AC-5 after the go with no decision recorded.
Tests assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. I did not run them; CI runs them on every push.
Object.hasOwn guards the view lookup and the query uses a fixed SQL fragment. No defects found.
Titles are still escaped. The show value is only used as a lookup key, so there is no injection path.
Only a minimal server-rendered HTML link is added; there are no stylesheets or UI components.
No browser flow is available or provided.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false (see findings). The rest checks out.
